title: Subpanel rough-in punch list
brief: A concise rough-in installation briefing and material check for an apprentice working on a commercial kitchen subpanel.

delegate.scenario: You are a lead journeyman electrician preparing the daily work plan for an apprentice wiring a commercial kitchen subpanel. The apprentice needs clear, sequential installation steps and a verified parts check before rough-in inspection tomorrow morning. The output must prevent costly rework and ensure strict compliance with National Electrical Code requirements.
delegate.inputs:
Panel: Subpanel B (Kitchen remodel, Oakview Diner).
Feed: 100A, 120/208V 3-phase from Main Switchboard, breaker 4.
Conduit run: 85 ft of 1-1/4" EMT already in place overhead.
Conductors listed in job tote:
- 3x #3 AWG THHN Copper (Line 1, Line 2, Line 3)
- 1x #8 AWG THHN Copper (Neutral)
- 1x #8 AWG bare Copper (Equipment Ground)
Scheduled kitchen equipment loads to land today:
- Walk-in cooler: 30A 208V 1-ph (needs 2-pole breaker, #10 AWG)
- Convection oven: 50A 208V 3-ph (needs 3-pole breaker, #6 AWG)
- Dishwasher booster heater: 40A 208V 3-ph (needs 3-pole breaker, #8 AWG)
- Handwash sink dedicated GFCI: 20A 120V 1-ph (needs 1-pole breaker, #12 AWG)
Notes from morning walk:
- Subpanel enclosure is NEMA 1 indoor surface mount.
- Main panel breaker 4 is tagged at 125A in the switchgear schedule.
delegate.goal: Provide the apprentice with an actionable step-by-step installation plan that flags discrepancies and ensures code-compliant panel assembly before tomorrow's inspection.

criteria.text: Specifies the target reader is an electrical apprentice needing clear sequential installation steps.
Requires a structured breakdown separating feeder verification, equipment branch circuits, and grounding details.
Instructs the AI to verify wire gauges and ampacity ratings against breaker sizes and code standards.
Limits the response to a single-page checklist or punch list format under 350 words.

traps.description: The feeder neutral wire is severely undersized for a 100A feeder serving 120V line-to-neutral loads.
Contradictory feeder overcurrent protection sizing between the job notes and the switchgear schedule.
